subject.title: [Bug]: Managed Memory Dreaming Promotion cron silently NO_REPLY since 2026-05-09 (jobs.json lastRun stays null)

question: How should managed Dreaming partial failures or no-op sweeps be surfaced after the SQLite-state migration: cron error/skipped/degraded status, cron diagnostics plus doctor/memory-status warnings, or plugin-local logs only?
rationale: Current source confirms the remaining visibility gap, but the right status semantics affect user alerts, retry/backoff behavior, and operator expectations, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Add degraded diagnostics
options.body: Record failed/no-op Dreaming sweep details in cron run diagnostics and doctor or memory status while preserving cron success for fully handled maintenance runs.

options.title: Make partial failures cron errors
options.body: Propagate failed workspaces to cron error status so existing cron alert/backoff machinery surfaces the problem aggressively.

options.title: Keep plugin-local logging
options.body: Treat the SQLite migration as sufficient and require users to inspect Memory Core logs for workspace-level Dreaming failures.

recommendation.title: Add degraded diagnostics
recommendation.body: Record failed/no-op Dreaming sweep details in cron run diagnostics and doctor or memory status while preserving cron success for fully handled maintenance runs.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent SQLite-state repair and related cleanup make steipete the best available owner to decide whether the remaining issue should stay cron-level or Memory Core diagnostic-level.
